Order 
This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. The applicant is apprehending his arrest in relation to Crime No.120/2024 registered at Police Station Garha, District Jabalpur, for the offence punishable under Sections 458, 409, 420, 384, 386,
323, 294, 506, 147, 148, 149 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
3. Learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the alleged offence.

It is further submitted that though an agreement to sale of a land got executed between the applicant and complainant, but since the complainant was failed to fulfill the terms and conditions of the agreement, therefore, the same lost its efficacy.

It is contended by learned counsel for NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:12745 2 MCRC-1935-2025 the applicant that the complaint contained the fact about the land which is part of agreement that the applicant is executing sale-deeds in favour of various persons and as such, an allegation of fraud has been alleged against the applicant.

In the complaint, it has also been alleged by the complainant that he has paid an amount to one of the co-accused namely Abdul Rajjak, who has assured him that the said amount shall be transferred to Manish Richhariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32372666/
1 the applicant, but according to him, the applicant has received nothing.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned Senior Advocate that if the whole dispute is seen, then it is clear that the dispute falls within the ambit of civil dispute.
He has further submitted that money, if any, paid by the complainant, has not been received by the applicant and under such circumstances, no case of alleged offence is made out against him.
It is further submitted that there is no cogent and plausible material available on record to show that the applicant, at any point of time, was involved in the alleged offence.
It is submitted that the applicant has not played any role in the alleged crime.
Even otherwise, it is contended that there is no evidence on record to indicate that the applicant attributed any deceptive role in the alleged offence.
On these submissions, it is prayed that the applicant may be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the submissions advanced on behalf of the applicant and submitted that looking to the contents of FIR, it is clear that it is a fraud in which the applicant has played an active role that too with the help of co-accused Abdul Rajjak, who is a known criminal and as such, looking to the nature of crime committed, the applicant is not entitled to get the protection of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12745 3 MCRC-1935-2025 anticipatory bail.
It is further submitted that money of the complainant has been embezzled by the applicant with the help of co-accused Abdul Rajjak and now, they are threatening the complainant.
It is, therefore, prayed that this application deserves to be dismissed.

5. Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of case diary, prima facie, I find substance in the submissions advanced by learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant.

Thus, without commenting anything on the merits of the case,
the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer/Arresting Officer of the Police Station concerned.
7. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 482(2) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
